title: JEE Main 2026 (April 2nd, Shift 2) - Mathematics - Quadratic Equations
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2 - 3x + r = 0$, and $\frac{\alpha}{2}, 2\beta$ be the roots of the equation $x^2 + 3x + r = 0$. If the roots of the equation $x^2 + 6x = m$ are $2\alpha + \beta + 2r$ and $\alpha - 2\beta - \frac{r}{2}$, then $m$ is equal to:
questions.explain:
Let $\alpha, \beta$ be roots of $x^2 - 3x + r = 0 \implies \alpha + \beta = 3$ and $\alpha\beta = r$.
Also, $\frac{\alpha}{2}, 2\beta$ are roots of $x^2 + 3x + r = 0 \implies \frac{\alpha}{2} + 2\beta = -3$ and $(\frac{\alpha}{2})(2\beta) = r \implies \alpha\beta = r$, which is consistent.
Solving the linear equations $\alpha + \beta = 3$ and $\alpha + 4\beta = -6$, we get $3\beta = -9 \implies \beta = -3$, and $\alpha = 6$. Then $r = -18$.
The given roots of $x^2 + 6x - m = 0$ are $r_1 = 2\alpha + \beta + 2r = 12 - 3 - 36 = -27$ and $r_2 = \alpha - 2\beta - \frac{r}{2} = 6 + 6 + 9 = 21$.
Notice that $r_1 + r_2 = -6$, matching the sum of roots. The product of roots is $-m = (-27)(21) = -567$, giving $m = 567$.
